summary:
## About Space Fire

**Space Fire** is an interactive data-driven platform developed by Team Sherlock Holmes for the NASA Space Apps Challenge.

Our project analyzes 384 historical NASA combustion experiments across 10 major NASA projects to understand how fire behaves in microgravity and how oxygen levels, airflow, and material types influence fire safety in spacecraft.

By combining data analysis, Power BI visualization, and an interactive Streamlit web application, we transform scattered NASA research into organized and accessible insights.

Our platform enables users to explore experiments, compare conditions, analyze fire behavior, and run What-If simulations to support better safety decisions.

**Our Goal:** To turn NASA's historical data into valuable insights that contribute to safer spacecraft and protect astronauts during future space missions.

SPACE FIRE – Project Details

Team Sherlock Holmes | NASA Space Apps Challenge

1. What Does Our Project Do and How Does It Work?

Space Fire is an interactive, data-driven platform designed to help researchers understand fire behavior in microgravity and improve spacecraft fire safety.

Our project brings together 384 historical NASA combustion experiments from 10 major NASA projects, including SAFFIRE and BASS-II, into one structured master dataset.

The platform works by organizing and analyzing experimental data to explore how different factors influence fire behavior in space, particularly oxygen concentration, airflow direction and velocity, and material types.

Users can interact with our Streamlit web application to filter experiments, explore raw data, access interactive Power BI visualizations, compare experimental conditions, and run What-If simulations to explore predicted burn times under different cabin conditions.

2. What Are the Benefits of the Project?

  • Makes decades of scattered NASA combustion research easier to access and understand.
  • Helps researchers identify patterns and relationships between environmental conditions and fire behavior.
  • Provides interactive tools for exploring and comparing experiments.
  • Allows users to investigate different cabin conditions through What-If simulations.
  • Supports more informed decisions regarding spacecraft fire safety.

3. What Is the Intended Impact?

Our main goal is to contribute to safer human space exploration.

By transforming historical experimental data into accessible and interactive insights, Space Fire aims to help researchers better understand fire risks in microgravity, identify potentially dangerous conditions, and support the development of improved spacecraft safety strategies.

Ultimately, we hope our platform can contribute to protecting astronauts and making future space missions safer.

4. What Tools, Programming Languages, Hardware, and Software Did We Use?

Our project combines data organization, visualization, and web application development.

  • Streamlit: Used to develop the interactive web application.
  • Power BI: Used to build interactive dashboards and analyze experimental data.
  • Structured Master Dataset: Used to consolidate and organize 384 NASA combustion experiments.
  • Artificial Intelligence: Incorporated into our platform's intelligent analysis vision to make research exploration and insight extraction more accessible.

The project presentation does not specify particular hardware or programming languages, so these are not listed as confirmed technologies.

5. How Is Our Project Creative and Innovative?

The creativity of Space Fire lies in transforming fragmented historical NASA research into a unified and interactive intelligence platform.

Instead of simply displaying experimental results, we connect multiple NASA combustion studies and make them explorable through interactive dashboards and What-If simulations.

This approach allows users to move beyond reading individual experiments and start exploring relationships between different experimental conditions, making complex scientific information easier to understand and investigate.

6. What Factors Did Our Team Consider?

Our team focused on the most important factors affecting fire behavior and safety in microgravity:

  • Microgravity: Understanding how the absence of normal buoyancy-driven airflow changes flame behavior.
  • Oxygen Concentration: Investigating how elevated oxygen levels influence material flammability.
  • Airflow: Considering airflow direction and velocity and their influence on combustion.
  • Material Types: Exploring how different materials respond to combustion conditions.
  • Data Accessibility: Bringing scattered historical experiments into one organized dataset.
  • Research Usability: Making scientific information accessible through interactive visualizations and simulations.

Our Final Vision

Space Fire is more than a data visualization project. It is an attempt to turn NASA's historical combustion research into practical knowledge that supports better understanding, smarter safety decisions, and safer future space exploration.
